first.rationale: The two measured declines this quarter are onboarding completion (-4%) and activation (-6%), which are the same funnel; simplify_onboarding is the direction with the most convergent inherited support (memory_86 on shortened onboarding lifting completion and time-to-value, memory_31 on signup field reduction producing a durable SMB activation lift, and memory_91 showing activation messaging compounds once accounts reach first action). It also attacks the competitor threat indirectly and more sustainably than discounting, by improving time-to-value rather than price. I am verifying memory_73 because promotional_pricing is the loudest candidate given the competitor's entry pricing, and its readout is explicitly caveated as pooling two cohorts after a mid-test redefinition — that is exactly the kind of defect that can manufacture an apparent acquisition/revenue lift, so I want the original record before either acting on it or ruling it out. I am verifying memory_86 because it is the direct evidential basis for my intended action and it is a day-52 consolidation whose underlying record I have not seen; if the completion lift there was measured on a cohort unlike today's, or if 'early product adoption' was a proxy rather than qualified revenue, my plan weakens and memory_31 becomes the primary support instead. I am not verifying memory_44 or memory_57 because enterprise_sales_assist and referral_incentive address neither of the two declining metrics nor the price-sensitive SMB segment under attack, so their accuracy does not change this week's choice. Downstream value risk: cutting onboarding steps can shed qualifying fields and data capture, importing lower-intent accounts that inflate activation counts while degrading qualified-revenue quality downstream — so the experiment must be gated on qualified-revenue and 30/60-day retention, not on completion rate alone. Standard experiment scale rather than broad rollout: the inherited evidence is real but it is prior-quarter and pre-competitor-entry, and the current declines may have a cause (competitive churn, mix shift) that onboarding changes do not touch. I hold the causal story as provisional; if verification shows memory_86 rests on a weak or redefined readout, I would fall back to memory_31's narrower signup-field change as a small_guarded_test rather than escalate.
